messages:
julie: FYI customer acme-prod reporting a burst of 504/502s from hosted API during a marketing spike. They hit timeouts while waiting for inference. Ticket: https://tickets/acme/3421 :grimacing:

simon: Can you paste a few gateway traces and any autoscaler events? Is this HPA+KEDA?

julie: Pasting a short sample from the gateway traces and keda events:
```
[gateway] 2026-03-15T21:02:12Z upstream request timed out -> 504, customer_req_id=abc123
[backend] 2026-03-15T21:02:14Z 502 Bad Gateway "no healthy upstream"
KEDA: ScaledObject acme-infer scaled to 0 due to cooldown window
KEDA: trigger metric: queueLength=0, cooldown=120s, minReplicaCount=0
```

luke: sounds like scale-to-zero + long model init -> coldstart timeouts. Do we see model init logs failing or taking >30s? Also check if KEDA target metric expression is returning 0 because requests are short-lived and never queue.

maria: Quick auth check — I see intermittent 401s in the same window in the auth logs, likely token rotate hitting the model pull step during scaleup. Snippet:
```
[auth] 2026-03-15T21:02:10Z token fetch failed: 401 unauthorized (rotated key)
[model-fetch] 2026-03-15T21:02:11Z retrying model download after auth failure
```

aj: Ran a few kubectl commands from the cluster during the incident:
```
# kubectl get hpa -n hosted acme-infer-hpa
NAME               REFERENCE              TARGETS   MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS   AGE
acme-infer-hpa     Deployment/acme-inf    0%/80%    0         10        0          3h

# kubectl get scaledobject -n hosted acme-infer-so -o yaml | grep -E "minReplica|cooldown|pollingInterval"
  minReplicaCount: 0
  cooldownPeriod: 120
  pollingInterval: 30
```

julie: So HPA min=0 + KEDA minReplicaCount=0 + cooldown 120s. Customer burst created many short-lived requests so KEDA never saw queue build-up, scaled to 0, on first request model init+auth took ~45s and the gateway timed out at 30s -> 504.

simon: Repro steps we should document for support: 1) simulate N concurrent requests that each spawn a cold model init (curl the hosted endpoint with a pinned large model) 2) observe KEDA scale events and gateway traces 3) reproduce 504 when model init > gateway timeout.

luke: Short-term mitigation: bump minReplicaCount to 1 for that tenant, or set HPA minPods=1. Medium: increase KEDA pollingInterval smaller? No — that just detects faster, but warmup still takes time. Better: implement a prewarm hook (annotation) to keep a warm replica for pinned models. Also increase gateway timeout to 60s as a temporary band-aid.

maria: Also make sure token rotation for that tenant isn't causing repeated 401s during init. Workaround: temporarily disable rotation window for the tenant while we exercise prewarm.

aj: I'll open a runbook PR with commands used and the exact kube patches. Commands we used to mitigate:
```bash
kubectl patch scaledobject acme-infer-so -n hosted --patch '{"spec":{"minReplicaCount":1}}'
kubectl patch hpa acme-infer-hpa -n hosted --patch '{"spec":{"minReplicas":1}}'
# and change gateway timeout: edit deployment gateway -> env GATEWAY_TIMEOUT=60s
```

julie: Customer notified, applied minReplicaCount=1 as a hotfix. They still want a root cause: KEDA+HPA misconfiguration + auth rotation during coldstart + long model init time.

ops-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-0315-AUTOSCALE-QUIESCE-1, severity=P2, assigned=eng-sre.

simon: Follow-ups: (1) add prewarm annotation/feature for pinned large models, (2) add a KEDA pattern doc for short-lived bursts explaining minReplica pitfalls, (3) add metric alert for model-init latency > 20s and auth-failure spikes during scaleups.

luke: I'll own the prewarm prototype. aj, can you take the runbook PR and the tenant-specific postmortem?

aj: yep — will do. :thumbsup:

julie: thanks everyone. closing loop with support ticket after postmortem. :eyes:
